## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 1 — Cover (01_cover.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Cover
- **Layout**: Dark background, centered
- **Title**: Are You Getting What You Pay For?
- **Subtitle**: Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs: Why Software Tests Fail and Hardware Attestation Wins
- **Tagline**: Commercial LLM APIs may silently serve cheaper models — current detection methods are fundamentally broken.
- **Reference**: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715
- **Date**: April 2026
- **Bottom**: CONFIDENTIAL

---

### Slide 2 — The Model Substitution Problem (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column (left: taxonomy diagram, right: hypothesis framework)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly replace advertised models with cheaper alternatives.
- **Left Column — Substitution Taxonomy** (4 dark cards, stacked):
  1. `{{ICON:server}}` **Smaller Model** — e.g., 8B instead of 70B
  2. `{{ICON:microchip}}` **Quantized Variant** — FP8/INT8 instead of FP16
  3. `{{ICON:chart-line}}` **Fine-tuned/Updated** — modified weights served silently
  4. `{{ICON:eye-slash}}` **Different Family** — entirely different architecture
- **Right Column — Hypothesis Framework**:
  - Formal framing: H₀: API serves P_spec(y|x) vs H₁: API serves P_actual(y|x)
  - Black-box API: only text outputs observable
  - `{{ICON:dollar}}` GPU cost savings = primary economic driver
  - `{{ICON:lock-closed}}` Black-box nature = zero verifiability for users
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 2/9

---

### Slide 3 — FP8 Quantization Preserves Accuracy (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width table
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: FP8 quantization barely degrades benchmark scores — differences often fall within error bars, making detection extremely challenging.
- **Table Title**: Benchmark Accuracy: Original vs FP8 Quantized Models
- **Table Data** (full table from source, 5 model pairs):

| Model | MMLU | GSM8K | MATH | GPQA Diamond |
|-------|------|-------|------|--------------|
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct | 62.69 ± 0.18 | 61.14 ± 3.47 | 20.65 ± 3.43 | 22.62 ± 0.22 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | 62.43 ± 0.26 | 60.90 ± 4.10 | 14.91 ± 2.49 | 20.14 ± 0.24 |
| Llama-3-70B-Instruct | 78.05 ± 0.08 | 88.06 ± 1.44 | 35.69 ± 1.33 | 29.60 ± 0.51 |
| Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8 | 77.88 ± 0.13 | 87.35 ± 1.24 | 35.75 ± 1.16 | 33.12 ± 0.30 |
| Gemma-2-9b-it | 71.86 ± 0.08 | 81.80 ± 1.35 | 33.41 ± 0.28 | 28.64 ± 2.97 |
| Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8 | 71.92 ± 0.11 | 79.41 ± 1.14 | 32.53 ± 0.34 | 27.81 ± 3.22 |
| Qwen2-72B-Instruct | 82.18 ± 0.08 | 86.72 ± 1.00 | 37.39 ± 1.41 | 29.93 ± 2.71 |
| Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8 | 81.98 ± 0.08 | 86.82 ± 0.97 | 37.67 ± 1.39 | 31.08 ± 1.96 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 59.15 ± 0.10 | 35.90 ± 4.54 | 8.94 ± 1.24 | 21.60 ± 0.17 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8 | 58.77 ± 0.13 | 32.20 ± 4.02 | 7.68 ± 1.23 | 22.72 ± 0.19 |

- **Visual highlight**: FP8 rows in slightly lighter background; annotation "within error bars" on MMLU/GSM8K columns
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 3/9

---

### Slide 4 — Temperature Scaling (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + top-section image (figure_1.jpg) + bottom text annotation
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Higher temperatures degrade all models uniformly — amplifying noise rather than revealing substitution signals.
- **Image**: `figure_1.jpg` — benchmark accuracy vs temperature for five models across four tasks (785×621, ratio 1.26)
- **Image placement**: Left 60% of content area, right-aligned annotation panel
- **Right annotation panel** (3 bullet points):
  - At temperature 2.0, performance degradation is universal across all model families
  - The gap between original and FP8 variant becomes noise-dominated at high temperatures
  - Tested at T = 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 — higher T obscures rather than reveals substitution
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715, Figure 1 | CONFIDENTIAL | 4/9

---

### Slide 5 — Log-Prob Nondeterminism (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width image (figure_5.jpg) + explanation below
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Production inference nondeterminism renders log-probability fingerprinting unreliable — auditors cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure variation from actual substitution.
- **Image**: `figure_5.jpg` — log probability variation across inference frameworks and hardware for Llama-3-8B (656×232, ratio 2.83, wide landscape)
- **Image placement**: Full-width top section of content area, ~280px height
- **Below image — two-column explanation**:
  - Left card: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` **Software Nondeterminism** — transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2 produce different log probabilities for the same model
  - Right card: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` **Hardware Nondeterminism** — A100 vs H100 GPUs produce measurably different log-prob distributions for identical model weights
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715, Figure 5 | CONFIDENTIAL | 5/9

---

### Slide 6 — Randomized Routing (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column (left: concept diagram, right: adversarial strategies)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Mixing substituted responses at low probability p → 0 makes statistical detection query-prohibitive; adversarial providers can always stay below the detection threshold.
- **Left Column — Randomized Routing Diagram**:
  - Visual: probability mixing diagram
  - Formula box: `P_mix(y|x) = (1-p)·P_spec + p·P_sub`
  - Arrow showing: as p → 0, P_mix → P_spec
  - Labels: "At p=0.1: ~10,000 queries needed" / "At p=0.01: ~1,000,000 queries needed"
  - Bottom note: Query budget grows exponentially as p decreases
- **Right Column — Adversarial Countermeasures** (2 cards):
  - `{{ICON:funnel}}` **Randomized Substitution** — Route fraction p of queries to cheaper model; detection requires impractically large query budgets as p → 0
  - `{{ICON:eye-slash}}` **Benchmark Evasion** — Detect known benchmark prompts and serve genuine model for audit traffic; substitute for regular traffic
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 6/9

---

### Slide 7 — Software Methods Summary (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width comparison matrix (3 rows × 4 columns)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: All three software-only auditing approaches share a fatal flaw: they are defeated by the very properties of production LLM deployment.
- **Matrix title**: Software-Only Auditing Methods: Failure Mode Analysis
- **Matrix columns**: Method Type | Core Mechanism | Fatal Weakness | Practical Limitation
- **Matrix rows**:

| Method Type | Core Mechanism | Fatal Weakness | Practical Limitation |
|-------------|---------------|----------------|---------------------|
| `{{ICON:chart-bar}}` Text-Based Statistical Tests (e.g., MMD) | Compare output text distributions between reference and API | Cannot distinguish subtle quantized variants; fails against partial/randomized substitutions | Requires impractically large query budgets (>10,000–1,000,000 queries) |
| `{{ICON:chart-line}}` Log-Probability Fingerprinting | Compare token-level log-probs to local reference model | Production nondeterminism from software versions (transformers, vLLM) and GPU hardware (A100 vs H100) creates indistinguishable variation | Auditors cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure from substitution |
| `{{ICON:triangle-exclamation}}` Adversarial Countermeasures (Active Evasion) | N/A — provider-side attack | Benchmark evasion: detect audit prompts and route to genuine model; randomized routing at low p defeats statistical power | Any software detection method can be actively circumvented by a motivated provider |

- **Bottom summary bar**: `{{ICON:shield-half}}` Conclusion: No software method provides reliable, query-efficient detection under adversarial conditions
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 7/9

---

### Slide 8 — TEE Solution (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column contrast (left: software methods, right: TEE)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Trusted Execution Environments provide cryptographic proof that specific model weights are loaded and executing — the only currently deployable solution with provable guarantees.
- **Left Column — Software Methods** (dark card with red accent, failure summary):
  - Header: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` Software Auditing: Fundamentally Unreliable
  - • Statistical tests: query-prohibitive
  - • Log-prob fingerprinting: defeated by nondeterminism
  - • Adversarial evasion: always possible
  - • ZKPs: computationally prohibitive for large models
- **Right Column — TEE Solution** (dark card with green accent):
  - Header: `{{ICON:shield-check}}` TEE Hardware Attestation: Provably Secure
  - `{{ICON:key}}` **Cryptographic attestation** — hardware-level proof of model weights and inference code
  - `{{ICON:microchip}}` **NVIDIA Confidential Computing** — H100 GPU TEE support available today
  - `{{ICON:badge-check}}` **Only modest performance overhead** — practical for production deployment
  - `{{ICON:checkmark}}` **Provable, efficient, robust** — defeats all substitution types
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 8/9

---

### Slide 9 — Key Takeaways (04_ending.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Ending / Takeaways
- **Layout**: Dark background, centered with structured takeaway list + call-to-action
- **Title**: Key Takeaways: Close the Verification Gap with Hardware Attestation
- **5 Takeaway Items** (numbered, gold numbers):
  1. `{{ICON:dollar}}` Model substitution is economically motivated — FP8 quantization cuts GPU costs while barely affecting benchmarks, making it an attractive and nearly undetectable swap.
  2. `{{ICON:chart-bar}}` Statistical text tests (MMD) require impractically large query budgets and fail against randomized or subtle substitutions.
  3. `{{ICON:chart-line}}` Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level nondeterminism across software frameworks and GPU hardware.
  4. `{{ICON:funnel}}` Randomized routing and benchmark evasion actively undermine all software-only detection — no query budget is sufficient.
  5. `{{ICON:shield-check}}` Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) are the only currently viable path to verifiable LLM API integrity — provable, deployable, and efficient.
- **Call-to-Action box**: The ML community should demand TEE-backed attestation as a standard requirement for commercial LLM API contracts.
- **Reference**: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715
- **Footer**: CONFIDENTIAL | 9/9

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

| **Total Duration** | ~20 minutes |
| **Notes Style** | Formal / technical |
| **Presentation Purpose** | Persuade + Inform |

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column (left: taxonomy diagram, right: hypothesis framework)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width table
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: FP8 quantization barely degrades benchmark scores — differences often fall within error bars, making detection extremely challenging.
- **Table Title**: Benchmark Accuracy: Original vs FP8 Quantized Models

- **Page Type**: Content

  - Tested at T = 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 — higher T obscures rather than reveals substitution
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715, Figure 1 | CONFIDENTIAL | 4/9

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width image (figure_5.jpg) + explanation below
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Production inference nondeterminism renders log-probability fingerprinting unreliable — auditors cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure variation from actual substitution.
- **Image**: `figure_5.jpg` — log probability variation across inference frameworks and hardware for Llama-3-8B (656×232, ratio 2.83, wide landscape)
- **Image placement**: Full-width top section of content area, ~280px height
- **Below image — two-column explanation**:
  - Left card: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` **Software Nondeterminism** — transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2 produce different log probabilities for the same model
  - Right card: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` **Hardware Nondeterminism** — A100 vs H100 GPUs produce measurably different log-prob distributions for identical model weights
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715, Figure 5 | CONFIDENTIAL | 5/9

---

### Slide 6 — Randomized Routing (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column (left: concept diagram, right: adversarial strategies)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Mixing substituted responses at low probability p → 0 makes statistical detection query-prohibitive; adversarial providers can always stay below the detection threshold.
- **Left Column — Randomized Routing Diagram**:
  - Visual: probability mixing diagram
  - Formula box: `P_mix(y|x) = (1-p)·P_spec + p·P_sub`
  - Arrow showing: as p → 0, P_mix → P_spec
  - Labels: "At p=0.1: ~10,000 queries needed" / "At p=0.01: ~1,000,000 queries needed"
  - Bottom note: Query budget grows exponentially as p decreases
- **Right Column — Adversarial Countermeasures** (2 cards):
  - `{{ICON:funnel}}` **Randomized Substitution** — Route fraction p of queries to cheaper model; detection requires impractically large query budgets as p → 0
  - `{{ICON:eye-slash}}` **Benchmark Evasion** — Detect known benchmark prompts and serve genuine model for audit traffic; substitute for regular traffic
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 6/9

---

### Slide 7 — Software Methods Summary (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + full-width comparison matrix (3 rows × 4 columns)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: All three software-only auditing approaches share a fatal flaw: they are defeated by the very properties of production LLM deployment.
- **Matrix title**: Software-Only Auditing Methods: Failure Mode Analysis
- **Matrix columns**: Method Type | Core Mechanism | Fatal Weakness | Practical Limitation
- **Matrix rows**:

| Method Type | Core Mechanism | Fatal Weakness | Practical Limitation |
|-------------|---------------|----------------|---------------------|
| `{{ICON:chart-bar}}` Text-Based Statistical Tests (e.g., MMD) | Compare output text distributions between reference and API | Cannot distinguish subtle quantized variants; fails against partial/randomized substitutions | Requires impractically large query budgets (>10,000–1,000,000 queries) |
| `{{ICON:chart-line}}` Log-Probability Fingerprinting | Compare token-level log-probs to local reference model | Production nondeterminism from software versions (transformers, vLLM) and GPU hardware (A100 vs H100) creates indistinguishable variation | Auditors cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure from substitution |
| `{{ICON:triangle-exclamation}}` Adversarial Countermeasures (Active Evasion) | N/A — provider-side attack | Benchmark evasion: detect audit prompts and route to genuine model; randomized routing at low p defeats statistical power | Any software detection method can be actively circumvented by a motivated provider |

- **Bottom summary bar**: `{{ICON:shield-half}}` Conclusion: No software method provides reliable, query-efficient detection under adversarial conditions
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 7/9

---

### Slide 8 — TEE Solution (03_content.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Content
- **Layout**: Exhibit key-message bar + two-column contrast (left: software methods, right: TEE)
- **Key Message (Exhibit Bar)**: Trusted Execution Environments provide cryptographic proof that specific model weights are loaded and executing — the only currently deployable solution with provable guarantees.
- **Left Column — Software Methods** (dark card with red accent, failure summary):
  - Header: `{{ICON:circle-x}}` Software Auditing: Fundamentally Unreliable
  - • Statistical tests: query-prohibitive
  - • Log-prob fingerprinting: defeated by nondeterminism
  - • Adversarial evasion: always possible
  - • ZKPs: computationally prohibitive for large models
- **Right Column — TEE Solution** (dark card with green accent):
  - Header: `{{ICON:shield-check}}` TEE Hardware Attestation: Provably Secure
  - `{{ICON:key}}` **Cryptographic attestation** — hardware-level proof of model weights and inference code
  - `{{ICON:microchip}}` **NVIDIA Confidential Computing** — H100 GPU TEE support available today
  - `{{ICON:badge-check}}` **Only modest performance overhead** — practical for production deployment
  - `{{ICON:checkmark}}` **Provable, efficient, robust** — defeats all substitution types
- **Footer**: Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 | CONFIDENTIAL | 8/9

---

### Slide 9 — Key Takeaways (04_ending.svg style)

- **Page Type**: Ending / Takeaways
- **Layout**: Dark background, centered with structured takeaway list + call-to-action
- **Title**: Key Takeaways: Close the Verification Gap with Hardware Attestation
- **5 Takeaway Items** (numbered, gold numbers):
  1. `{{ICON:dollar}}` Model substitution is economically motivated — FP8 quantization cuts GPU costs while barely affecting benchmarks, making it an attractive and nearly undetectable swap.
  2. `{{ICON:chart-bar}}` Statistical text tests (MMD) require impractically large query budgets and fail against randomized or subtle substitutions.
  3. `{{ICON:chart-line}}` Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level nondeterminism across software frameworks and GPU hardware.
  4. `{{ICON:funnel}}` Randomized routing and benchmark evasion actively undermine all software-only detection — no query budget is sufficient.
  5. `{{ICON:shield-check}}` Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) are the only currently viable path to verifiable LLM API integrity — provable, deployable, and efficient.
- **Call-to-Action box**: The ML community should demand TEE-backed attestation as a standard requirement for commercial LLM API contracts.

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

  <text x="58" y="57" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Higher temperatures degrade all models uniformly — amplifying noise rather than revealing substitution signals.</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="96" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">Higher Temperature Amplifies Performance Gaps but Increases Noise</text>

  <text x="40" y="118" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">BENCHMARK ACCURACY vs TEMPERATURE — FIVE MODELS, FOUR TASKS</text>

  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-gradient)"/>

  <rect x="40" y="14" width="1200" height="56" fill="#0D1117"/>

  <text x="58" y="57" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Production inference nondeterminism renders log-probability fingerprinting unreliable — legitimate variance is indistinguishable from substitution.</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="96" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">Log Probability Fingerprinting Fails Due to Inference Nondeterminism</text>
  <text x="40" y="116" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">LLAMA-3-8B: LOG-PROB VARIATION ACROSS FRAMEWORKS AND HARDWARE</text>

  <!-- Container: full width, ~320px height maintains aspect ratio for 1200 wide -->
  <rect x="40" y="126" width="1200" height="270" fill="#F8F9FA" rx="4" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <image href="../images/figure_5.jpg" x="44" y="130" width="1192" height="262" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/>

  <text x="640" y="408" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Figure 5: Log-probability variation for the same Llama-3-8B model across different inference frameworks and GPU hardware</text>

  <!-- ===== BOTTOM: Two-column explanation ===== -->

  <!-- Left card: Software Nondeterminism -->
  <rect x="40" y="420" width="585" height="200" fill="#FEE2E2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="420" width="5" height="200" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-x" x="58" y="436" width="28" height="28" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="100" y="454" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Software Nondeterminism</text>
  <text x="58" y="480" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">The same Llama-3-8B model weights produce</text>
  <text x="58" y="500" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">measurably different log probabilities depending</text>
  <text x="58" y="520" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">on the inference framework version:</text>
  <text x="58" y="546" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">• transformers 4.40 vs transformers 4.50</text>
  <text x="58" y="566" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">• vLLM 0.6.2 vs vLLM 0.8.2</text>
  <text x="58" y="596" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Framework version updates introduce floating-point</text>
  <text x="58" y="612" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">arithmetic divergence even with identical weights</text>

  <!-- Right card: Hardware Nondeterminism -->
  <rect x="655" y="420" width="585" height="200" fill="#FEE2E2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="655" y="420" width="5" height="200" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-x" x="673" y="436" width="28" height="28" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="715" y="454" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Hardware Nondeterminism</text>
  <text x="673" y="480" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">Different GPU microarchitectures produce different</text>
  <text x="673" y="500" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">log-probability distributions for identical model</text>
  <text x="673" y="520" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">weights and inference code:</text>
  <text x="673" y="546" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">• NVIDIA A100 vs NVIDIA H100</text>
  <text x="673" y="566" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">• Tensor core implementations differ</text>
  <text x="673" y="596" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">An auditor's local A100 reference cannot reliably</text>
  <text x="673" y="612" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">compare against a provider's H100 deployment</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="636" x2="1240" y2="636" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="660" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715, Figure 5</text>
  <text x="640" y="660" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="660" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">5 / 9</text>
</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">

      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>

      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>

  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-gradient)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="1200" height="56" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="5" height="56" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="37" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">KEY FINDING</text>
  <text x="58" y="57" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Mixing substituted responses at low probability p → 0 makes statistical detection query-prohibitive; adversarial providers can always evade below the detection threshold.</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="96" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">Randomized Routing at Low Rates Makes Statistical Detection Query-Prohibitive</text>

  <!-- ===== LEFT COLUMN: Probability Mixing Diagram ===== -->
  <text x="48" y="122" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">RANDOMIZED SUBSTITUTION MODEL</text>

  <!-- Formula box -->
  <rect x="48" y="130" width="580" height="70" fill="#111827" rx="8"/>
  <text x="340" y="158" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold">P_mix(y|x) = (1−p)·P_spec + p·P_sub</text>
  <text x="340" y="185" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">As p → 0, the mixed distribution converges to the specified model</text>

  <!-- Routing diagram -->
  <!-- User queries box -->
  <rect x="48" y="218" width="160" height="60" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <text x="128" y="244" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">User</text>
  <text x="128" y="262" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Queries</text>

  <!-- Arrow to router -->
  <line x1="208" y1="248" x2="268" y2="248" stroke="#374151" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="268,243 278,248 268,253" fill="#374151"/>

  <!-- Router box -->
  <rect x="278" y="218" width="120" height="60" fill="#374151" rx="8"/>
  <text x="338" y="244" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Provider</text>
  <text x="338" y="262" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Router</text>

  <!-- Arrow to genuine (top, 1-p) -->
  <line x1="398" y1="228" x2="458" y2="200" stroke="#10B981" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="450,196 462,198 455,207" fill="#10B981"/>
  <text x="430" y="216" fill="#10B981" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">1−p</text>

  <!-- Arrow to substitute (bottom, p) -->
  <line x1="398" y1="268" x2="458" y2="296" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="450,296 462,294 455,305" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="405" y="292" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">p</text>

  <!-- Genuine model box -->
  <rect x="462" y="176" width="160" height="52" fill="#065F46" rx="8"/>
  <text x="542" y="199" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Genuine Model</text>
  <text x="542" y="216" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6EE7B7" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">P_spec(y|x)</text>

  <!-- Substitute model box -->
  <rect x="462" y="280" width="160" height="52" fill="#7F1D1D" rx="8"/>
  <text x="542" y="303" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Substitute Model</text>
  <text x="542" y="320" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FCA5A5" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">P_sub(y|x)</text>

  <!-- Query budget table -->
  <text x="48" y="360" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Query Budget Required for Reliable Detection</text>
  <rect x="48" y="370" width="580" height="32" fill="#1E40AF" rx="4"/>
  <text x="68" y="391" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Substitution Rate (p)</text>
  <text x="360" y="391" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Approx. Queries Needed</text>
  <text x="540" y="391" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Feasibility</text>

  <rect x="48" y="402" width="580" height="30" fill="#F8F9FA"/>
  <text x="68" y="422" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.5 (50% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="422" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~100 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="422" text-anchor="middle" fill="#10B981" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Possible</text>

  <rect x="48" y="432" width="580" height="30" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="68" y="452" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.1 (10% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="452" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~10,000 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="452" text-anchor="middle" fill="#F59E0B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Expensive</text>

  <rect x="48" y="462" width="580" height="30" fill="#F8F9FA"/>
  <text x="68" y="482" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.01 (1% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="482" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~1,000,000 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="482" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Infeasible</text>

  <rect x="48" y="492" width="580" height="30" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="68" y="512" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p → 0 (near-undetectable)</text>
  <text x="360" y="512" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">→ ∞</text>
  <text x="540" y="512" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Impossible</text>

  <!-- Key insight note -->
  <rect x="48" y="532" width="580" height="60" fill="#111827" rx="6"/>
  <text x="68" y="556" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Query budget grows as O(1/p²) — providers can always</text>
  <text x="68" y="576" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">choose p small enough to defeat any fixed query budget.</text>
