  <line x1="398" y1="228" x2="458" y2="200" stroke="#10B981" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="450,196 462,198 455,207" fill="#10B981"/>
  <text x="430" y="216" fill="#10B981" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">1−p</text>

  <!-- Arrow to substitute (bottom, p) -->
  <line x1="398" y1="268" x2="458" y2="296" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="450,296 462,294 455,305" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="405" y="292" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">p</text>

  <!-- Genuine model box -->
  <rect x="462" y="176" width="160" height="52" fill="#065F46" rx="8"/>
  <text x="542" y="199" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Genuine Model</text>
  <text x="542" y="216" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6EE7B7" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">P_spec(y|x)</text>

  <!-- Substitute model box -->
  <rect x="462" y="280" width="160" height="52" fill="#7F1D1D" rx="8"/>
  <text x="542" y="303" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Substitute Model</text>
  <text x="542" y="320" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FCA5A5" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">P_sub(y|x)</text>

  <!-- Query budget table -->
  <text x="48" y="360" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Query Budget Required for Reliable Detection</text>
  <rect x="48" y="370" width="580" height="32" fill="#1E40AF" rx="4"/>
  <text x="68" y="391" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Substitution Rate (p)</text>
  <text x="360" y="391" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Approx. Queries Needed</text>
  <text x="540" y="391" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Feasibility</text>

  <rect x="48" y="402" width="580" height="30" fill="#F8F9FA"/>
  <text x="68" y="422" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.5 (50% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="422" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~100 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="422" text-anchor="middle" fill="#10B981" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Possible</text>

  <rect x="48" y="432" width="580" height="30" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="68" y="452" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.1 (10% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="452" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~10,000 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="452" text-anchor="middle" fill="#F59E0B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Expensive</text>

  <rect x="48" y="462" width="580" height="30" fill="#F8F9FA"/>
  <text x="68" y="482" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p = 0.01 (1% substitute)</text>
  <text x="360" y="482" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">~1,000,000 queries</text>
  <text x="540" y="482" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Infeasible</text>

  <rect x="48" y="492" width="580" height="30" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="68" y="512" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">p → 0 (near-undetectable)</text>
  <text x="360" y="512" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">→ ∞</text>
  <text x="540" y="512" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Impossible</text>

  <!-- Key insight note -->
  <rect x="48" y="532" width="580" height="60" fill="#111827" rx="6"/>
  <text x="68" y="556" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Query budget grows as O(1/p²) — providers can always</text>
  <text x="68" y="576" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">choose p small enough to defeat any fixed query budget.</text>

  <!-- Vertical divider -->
  <line x1="655" y1="110" x2="655" y2="630" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- ===== RIGHT COLUMN: Adversarial Countermeasures ===== -->
  <text x="675" y="122" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">ADVERSARIAL COUNTERMEASURES</text>

  <!-- Card: Randomized Substitution -->
  <rect x="675" y="130" width="565" height="210" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="675" y="130" width="5" height="210" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="funnel" x="694" y="148" width="26" height="26" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="732" y="164" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Randomized Substitution</text>
  <text x="694" y="192" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Route only a fraction p of user queries to the cheaper</text>
  <text x="694" y="212" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">substitute model, while serving the genuine model for</text>
  <text x="694" y="232" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">the remaining (1−p) fraction.</text>
  <text x="694" y="260" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">As p decreases, the mixed distribution P_mix converges</text>
  <text x="694" y="278" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">to P_spec — making the substitution statistically</text>
  <text x="694" y="296" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">indistinguishable from serving the genuine model.</text>
  <text x="694" y="324" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Result: Requires exponentially more queries for detection.</text>

  <!-- Card: Benchmark Evasion -->
  <rect x="675" y="356" width="565" height="210" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="675" y="356" width="5" height="210" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="eye-slash" x="694" y="374" width="26" height="26" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="732" y="390" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Benchmark Evasion</text>
  <text x="694" y="418" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Detect known benchmark prompts (MMLU, GSM8K,</text>
  <text x="694" y="438" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">MATH, etc.) and route them to the genuine model,</text>
  <text x="694" y="458" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">while serving substitutes for regular traffic.</text>
  <text x="694" y="486" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Benchmark prompts have known signatures and can be</text>
  <text x="694" y="506" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">fingerprinted by semantic similarity or exact match —</text>
  <text x="694" y="526" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">making audit-specific queries ineffective.</text>
  <text x="694" y="550" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Result: Audit traffic gets genuine model; real traffic gets substitute.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="652" x2="1240" y2="652" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="678" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715</text>
  <text x="640" y="678" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="678" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">6 / 9</text>
</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="top-gradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-gradient)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="1200" height="56" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="5" height="56" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="37" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">CONCLUSION</text>
  <text x="58" y="57" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">All three software-only auditing approaches share a fatal flaw: they are defeated by the very properties of production LLM deployment.</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="96" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">Software-Only Auditing Methods Are Fundamentally Unreliable</text>
  <text x="40" y="116" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="2">FAILURE MODE ANALYSIS MATRIX</text>

  <!-- Matrix container -->
  <rect x="40" y="126" width="1200" height="460" fill="#F8F9FA" rx="4"/>

  <!-- Matrix header row -->
  <rect x="40" y="126" width="1200" height="40" fill="#111827" rx="4"/>
  <text x="170" y="151" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">METHOD TYPE</text>
  <text x="480" y="151" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">CORE MECHANISM</text>
  <text x="790" y="151" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">FATAL WEAKNESS</text>
  <text x="1085" y="151" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">PRACTICAL LIMITATION</text>

  <!-- Column separators -->
  <line x1="300" y1="126" x2="300" y2="586" stroke="#374151" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="660" y1="126" x2="660" y2="586" stroke="#374151" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="930" y1="126" x2="930" y2="586" stroke="#374151" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- ===== ROW 1: Text-Based Statistical Tests ===== -->
  <rect x="40" y="166" width="1200" height="130" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Method name cell -->
  <rect x="40" y="166" width="260" height="130" fill="#FEF3C7"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="60" y="186" width="28" height="28" fill="#D97706"/>
  <text x="100" y="200" fill="#92400E" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Text-Based</text>
  <text x="60" y="220" fill="#92400E" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Statistical Tests</text>
  <text x="60" y="244" fill="#78350F" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">e.g., Maximum Mean</text>
  <text x="60" y="260" fill="#78350F" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Discrepancy (MMD)</text>
  <text x="60" y="284" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Text output distribution</text>

  <!-- Core mechanism cell -->
  <text x="320" y="190" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Compare text output distributions</text>
  <text x="320" y="210" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">between a local reference model</text>
  <text x="320" y="230" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">and the API responses using</text>
  <text x="320" y="250" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">hypothesis tests (e.g., MMD).</text>
  <text x="320" y="278" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Requires large sample sizes to</text>
  <text x="320" y="295" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">reach statistical significance.</text>

  <!-- Fatal weakness cell -->
  <rect x="665" y="170" width="260" height="122" fill="#FFF8F8"/>
  <text x="680" y="193" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Cannot detect subtle variants</text>
  <text x="680" y="213" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">FP8 quantization keeps output</text>
  <text x="680" y="231" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">distribution nearly identical —</text>
  <text x="680" y="249" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">differences fall within noise.</text>
  <text x="680" y="273" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Randomized substitution at</text>
  <text x="680" y="291" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">small p is undetectable.</text>

  <!-- Practical limitation cell -->
  <text x="948" y="193" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Requires 10,000–1,000,000+</text>
  <text x="948" y="211" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">API queries — cost-prohibitive</text>
  <text x="948" y="229" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">for continuous monitoring.</text>
  <text x="948" y="253" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Not practical at provider scale.</text>
  <text x="948" y="273" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Even large budgets defeated</text>
  <text x="948" y="291" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">by randomized routing.</text>

  <!-- Row separator -->
  <line x1="40" y1="296" x2="1240" y2="296" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- ===== ROW 2: Log-Probability Fingerprinting ===== -->
  <rect x="40" y="296" width="1200" height="130" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Method name cell -->
  <rect x="40" y="296" width="260" height="130" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-line" x="60" y="316" width="28" height="28" fill="#2563EB"/>
  <text x="100" y="330" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Log-Probability</text>
  <text x="60" y="350" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Fingerprinting</text>
  <text x="60" y="374" fill="#1D4ED8" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Token-level log-prob</text>
  <text x="60" y="390" fill="#1D4ED8" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">comparison via API</text>
  <text x="60" y="414" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Metadata-based method</text>

  <!-- Core mechanism cell -->
  <text x="320" y="320" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Compare token-level log-probs</text>
  <text x="320" y="340" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">from a local reference model</text>
  <text x="320" y="360" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">against API log-prob outputs.</text>
  <text x="320" y="384" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Uses fine-grained probability</text>
  <text x="320" y="402" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">distributions as a "fingerprint"</text>
  <text x="320" y="420" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">of the model's identity.</text>

  <!-- Fatal weakness cell -->
  <rect x="665" y="300" width="260" height="122" fill="#FFF8F8"/>
  <text x="680" y="323" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Production nondeterminism</text>
  <text x="680" y="343" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Same weights produce different</text>
  <text x="680" y="361" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">log-probs on: transformers 4.40</text>
  <text x="680" y="379" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2,</text>
  <text x="680" y="397" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">A100 vs H100 GPUs.</text>
  <text x="680" y="419" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Legitimate variance ≈ substitution signal</text>

  <!-- Practical limitation cell -->
  <text x="948" y="320" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Auditor's local reference cannot</text>
  <text x="948" y="338" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">match provider infrastructure —</text>
  <text x="948" y="356" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">different hardware guarantees</text>
  <text x="948" y="374" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">different log-prob values.</text>
  <text x="948" y="398" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Cannot distinguish infrastructure</text>
  <text x="948" y="416" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">variation from substitution.</text>

  <!-- Row separator -->
  <line x1="40" y1="426" x2="1240" y2="426" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- ===== ROW 3: Adversarial Countermeasures ===== -->
  <rect x="40" y="426" width="1200" height="130" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Method name cell -->
  <rect x="40" y="426" width="260" height="130" fill="#FEF2F2"/>
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="60" y="446" width="28" height="28" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="100" y="460" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Adversarial</text>
  <text x="60" y="480" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Countermeasures</text>
  <text x="60" y="504" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Active provider-side</text>
  <text x="60" y="520" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">evasion attacks</text>
  <text x="60" y="544" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Not a detection method</text>

  <!-- Core mechanism cell -->
  <text x="320" y="450" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Provider actively detects and</text>
  <text x="320" y="470" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">evades audit attempts: benchmark</text>
  <text x="320" y="490" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">evasion + randomized routing.</text>
  <text x="320" y="514" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Targets the detection method</text>
  <text x="320" y="532" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">itself rather than the model</text>
  <text x="320" y="550" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">distribution.</text>

  <!-- Fatal weakness cell -->
  <rect x="665" y="430" width="260" height="122" fill="#FFF8F8"/>
  <text x="680" y="453" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Undermines all methods</text>
  <text x="680" y="473" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Benchmark prompts can be</text>
  <text x="680" y="491" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">fingerprinted; audit-specific</text>

  <text x="60" y="260" fill="#78350F" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Discrepancy (MMD)</text>
  <text x="60" y="284" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Text output distribution</text>

  <!-- Core mechanism cell -->
  <text x="320" y="190" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Compare text output distributions</text>
  <text x="320" y="210" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">between a local reference model</text>
  <text x="320" y="230" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">and the API responses using</text>
  <text x="320" y="250" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">hypothesis tests (e.g., MMD).</text>
  <text x="320" y="278" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Requires large sample sizes to</text>
  <text x="320" y="295" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">reach statistical significance.</text>

  <!-- Fatal weakness cell -->
  <rect x="665" y="170" width="260" height="122" fill="#FFF8F8"/>

  <text x="680" y="213" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">FP8 quantization keeps output</text>
  <text x="680" y="231" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">distribution nearly identical —</text>
  <text x="680" y="249" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">differences fall within noise.</text>
  <text x="680" y="273" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Randomized substitution at</text>
  <text x="680" y="291" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">small p is undetectable.</text>

  <text x="948" y="291" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">by randomized routing.</text>

  <text x="320" y="340" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">from a local reference model</text>

  <text x="948" y="356" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">different hardware guarantees</text>
  <text x="948" y="374" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">different log-prob values.</text>
  <text x="948" y="398" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Cannot distinguish infrastructure</text>
  <text x="948" y="416" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">variation from substitution.</text>

  <!-- Row separator -->

  <!-- ===== ROW 3: Adversarial Countermeasures ===== -->

  <text x="60" y="480" fill="#991B1B" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Countermeasures</text>
  <text x="60" y="504" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Active provider-side</text>
  <text x="60" y="520" fill="#7F1D1D" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">evasion attacks</text>

  <text x="320" y="490" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">evasion + randomized routing.</text>
  <text x="320" y="514" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Targets the detection method</text>
  <text x="320" y="532" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">itself rather than the model</text>
  <text x="320" y="550" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">distribution.</text>

  <text x="640" y="52" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">Key Takeaways: Close the Verification Gap with Hardware Attestation</text>

  <!-- Gold divider -->
  <line x1="200" y1="68" x2="1080" y2="68" stroke="#D4AF37" stroke-width="2"/>

  <!-- ===== Takeaway Items ===== -->

  <!-- Takeaway 1 -->
  <rect x="40" y="82" width="1200" height="84" fill="#111827" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="82" width="5" height="84" fill="#D97706" rx="2"/>
  <text x="76" y="118" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">1</text>
  <use data-icon="dollar" x="114" y="96" width="22" height="22" fill="#D97706"/>
  <text x="148" y="112" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Model substitution is economically motivated and nearly undetectable via software</text>
  <text x="148" y="132" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">FP8 quantization cuts GPU costs significantly while keeping benchmark scores within error bars of the original model.</text>
  <text x="148" y="156" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Providers have clear financial incentives; users have zero visibility into what is actually being served.</text>

  <!-- Takeaway 2 -->
  <rect x="40" y="174" width="1200" height="70" fill="#111827" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="174" width="5" height="70" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <text x="76" y="206" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">2</text>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="114" y="184" width="22" height="22" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="148" y="200" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Statistical text tests (e.g., MMD) require impractically large query budgets</text>
  <text x="148" y="220" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Detection requires 10,000–1,000,000+ queries; randomized routing at small p makes any fixed budget insufficient.</text>
  <text x="148" y="238" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Query budget grows as O(1/p²) — providers can always choose p small enough to remain undetected.</text>

  <!-- Takeaway 3 -->
  <rect x="40" y="252" width="1200" height="70" fill="#111827" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="252" width="5" height="70" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <text x="76" y="284" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">3</text>
  <use data-icon="chart-line" x="114" y="262" width="22" height="22" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="148" y="278" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level nondeterminism</text>
  <text x="148" y="298" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Same weights produce different log-probs on transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2, A100 vs H100.</text>
  <text x="148" y="316" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Auditors cannot distinguish legitimate infrastructure variation from actual model substitution.</text>

  <!-- Takeaway 4 -->
  <rect x="40" y="330" width="1200" height="70" fill="#111827" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="330" width="5" height="70" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <text x="76" y="362" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">4</text>
  <use data-icon="funnel" x="114" y="340" width="22" height="22" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="148" y="356" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Randomized routing and benchmark evasion actively undermine all software detection</text>
  <text x="148" y="376" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Motivated providers can fingerprint audit traffic and apply benchmark evasion, making audits trivially defeatable.</text>
  <text x="148" y="394" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">This is an adversarial game where defenders are at a structural disadvantage in black-box API settings.</text>

  <!-- Takeaway 5 -->
  <rect x="40" y="408" width="1200" height="70" fill="#1A3320" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="408" width="5" height="70" fill="#10B981" rx="2"/>
  <text x="76" y="440" fill="#10B981" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">5</text>
  <use data-icon="shield-check" x="114" y="418" width="22" height="22" fill="#10B981"/>
  <text x="148" y="434" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Trusted Execution Environments are the only currently viable path to verifiable LLM APIs</text>
  <text x="148" y="454" fill="#6EE7B7" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">TEEs provide cryptographic attestation of model weights and inference code — NVIDIA H100 support is deployable today.</text>
  <text x="148" y="472" fill="#A7F3D0" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Provable, efficient (modest overhead), and robust against all substitution types.</text>

  <!-- Gold divider before CTA -->
  <line x1="200" y1="492" x2="1080" y2="492" stroke="#D4AF37" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Call to Action box -->
  <rect x="150" y="504" width="980" height="70" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="150" y="504" width="5" height="70" fill="#D4AF37" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="lightbulb" x="172" y="520" width="24" height="24" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="210" y="535" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">CALL TO ACTION</text>
  <text x="210" y="556" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">The ML community should demand TEE-backed attestation as a standard requirement in commercial LLM API contracts.</text>
  <text x="210" y="568" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Model integrity guarantees should be cryptographic, not contractual.</text>

  <!-- Reference -->
  <text x="640" y="600" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715 · Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="200" y1="626" x2="1080" y2="626" stroke="#1F2937" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="640" y="660" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">CONFIDENTIAL · © 2026 ML Security Research</text>
  <text x="1240" y="660" text-anchor="end" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">9 / 9</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

This presentation addresses a fundamental trust gap in commercial LLM APIs — one that affects every organization building on top of third-party model providers. [Pause]

The question is simple: when you pay for access to a specific model, are you actually getting that model? The answer, as we'll show, is: you can't currently know for certain.

Key points: (1) Model substitution is economically motivated and structurally enabled by black-box APIs (2) The research formalizes this as a hypothesis testing problem (3) The deck shows why all software detection methods fail, and proposes TEEs as the only viable solution
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_substitution_threat

[Transition] Let's establish the threat model precisely. There are four distinct substitution types a provider might use.

The formal framing matters: this is a hypothesis testing problem — H₀ says the API serves the advertised distribution, H₁ says it serves something else. [Data] The auditor only observes text outputs. No weights, no logits by default, no code. [Pause]

The economic driver is straightforward: GPU inference costs are significant, and serving an 8B model instead of a 70B, or an FP8 quantized variant instead of FP16, can dramatically reduce per-query costs — while billing remains unchanged. [Benchmark] The black-box nature of APIs means this substitution is the structural default, not an edge case.

[Scan Room] This framing — four substitution types, one hypothesis test, zero verifiability — sets up everything that follows.

Key points: (1) Four substitution types with different detectability profiles (2) Hypothesis testing framing: only text outputs observable (3) Economic incentives are strong and structural
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_quantization_benchmark

[Transition] The most dangerous substitution type is quantization — because the data shows it's nearly invisible.

Look at this table carefully. For Llama-3-70B, the MMLU drop from FP16 to FP8 is just 0.17 percentage points — well within the ± 0.08–0.13 error bars. [Data] For Qwen2-72B on GSM8K, the FP8 variant actually scores 0.10 points *higher* than the original. [Pause]

The only model where we see a clearly notable drop is Llama-3-8B on MATH — from 20.65 to 14.91. But even that difference would require thousands of benchmark queries to detect statistically.

[Benchmark] Most FP8 scores fall within the original model's ± standard deviation. From a statistical detection standpoint, this is not a signal — it's noise.

Key points: (1) FP8 quantization preserves benchmark performance almost completely (2) Differences often within error bars — statistically indistinguishable (3) This makes FP8 substitution economically attractive AND nearly undetectable
Duration: 2.5 minutes
Flex: [If time tight, point to Llama-70B row as representative example and move on]

---

# 04_temperature_scaling

[Transition] One might wonder: could we improve detection by varying the sampling temperature to amplify differences? The answer is no — and here's the empirical evidence.

[Data] Figure 1 shows benchmark accuracy versus temperature at 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 for all five model families across all four benchmarks. The pattern is consistent: at T=2.0, performance collapses across the board — for both original and FP8 variants equally. [Pause]

The gap between original and substitute does not widen at higher temperatures. Instead, variance increases so much that both models become statistically indistinguishable from random noise. Higher temperature amplifies the noise floor, not the signal.

[Benchmark] This eliminates temperature manipulation as a viable detection strategy. The substitution signal remains buried regardless of temperature choice.

Key points: (1) High temperature degrades all models uniformly (2) Gap between original and FP8 becomes noise-dominated at T=2.0 (3) Temperature manipulation provides no detection advantage
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_log_prob_nondeterminism

[Transition] Perhaps we can use more granular information — token-level log probabilities — as a model fingerprint? Figure 5 shows why this approach also fails in production.

[Data] The same Llama-3-8B model, with identical weights, produces measurably different log-probability distributions when served by transformers 4.40 versus 4.50, and by vLLM 0.6.2 versus 0.8.2. The same is true when comparing A100 versus H100 GPU inference. [Pause]

This is not a minor calibration issue. The variation introduced by software versions and GPU microarchitectures is of comparable magnitude to the variation an auditor would expect from a model substitution.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication: an auditor's local reference machine will never match a provider's exact production stack — different hardware, different framework versions, different CUDA libraries. The fingerprint is not stable across environments.

Key points: (1) Software framework versions introduce non-trivial log-prob variation (2) GPU hardware (A100 vs H100) introduces additional nondeterminism (3) Production variation is indistinguishable from substitution signal
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_randomized_routing

[Transition] Even if we could overcome both the benchmark precision problem and the nondeterminism problem, adversarial providers have active countermeasures that defeat any query-based approach.

The first is randomized substitution. The formula is simple: P_mix = (1-p)·P_spec + p·P_sub. [Data] As p approaches zero, the mixed distribution converges to the specified model's distribution — making it statistically indistinguishable without exponentially more queries. [Pause]

[Benchmark] At p=0.1, you need roughly 10,000 queries. At p=0.01, you need roughly 1 million. At p→0, no fixed query budget is sufficient. Providers can always choose p small enough to stay below any detection threshold.

The second countermeasure is benchmark evasion: detect audit-specific prompts by semantic similarity and route them to the genuine model. Regular traffic gets the substitute.

Key points: (1) Randomized routing makes detection query-prohibitive as p→0 (2) O(1/p²) query budget growth — always defeatable (3) Benchmark evasion targets the detection mechanism itself
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 07_software_methods_summary

[Transition] We've now examined all three software-based detection approaches individually. This matrix puts them side by side to show the common structural failure.

Text-based statistical tests fail because FP8 outputs are nearly indistinguishable, and randomized routing defeats any fixed query budget. Log-probability fingerprinting fails because production nondeterminism makes legitimate variation indistinguishable from substitution. And all methods are rendered moot by adversarial countermeasures that any motivated provider can deploy. [Pause]

[Benchmark] The conclusion is not that these methods are poorly designed — they are reasonable attempts given the constraints. The conclusion is that the constraint itself — relying on observable outputs from a black-box API — is fundamentally incompatible with the security guarantee required.

[Scan Room] This sets up the question: if software methods cannot work, what can?

Key points: (1) Three failure modes, each independently fatal (2) Adversarial countermeasures compound all three (3) The fundamental constraint is the black-box API architecture, not the specific method
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_tee_solution

[Transition] The answer is to exit the software-only paradigm entirely. Trusted Execution Environments solve the problem at the architectural level.

A TEE — specifically NVIDIA Confidential Computing on H100 GPUs — creates a hardware-secured enclave. The provider runs inference inside the enclave, and the hardware generates a cryptographic attestation proving that specific model weights are loaded and specific inference code is executing. [Pause]

[Data] Unlike ZKPs, which are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale — they would take hours to verify a single inference pass — TEEs introduce only modest performance overhead. They are deployable today.

[Benchmark] The critical difference from all software methods: TEE attestation is not statistical evidence, it is cryptographic proof. A motivated provider cannot fake it. Hardware enforces what contracts cannot.

Key points: (1) TEEs provide cryptographic, not statistical, proof of model identity (2) NVIDIA H100 Confidential Computing is available today (3) Modest overhead — practical for production (4) Defeats all four substitution types
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 09_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five takeaways that I'd ask you to carry out of this room.

One: model substitution is economically motivated and structurally enabled. This is not a hypothetical threat — it's a rational business decision under current API architecture.

Two through four: every software detection method has a fatal weakness. Statistical tests need impractical query budgets. Log-prob fingerprinting is broken by production nondeterminism. Adversarial countermeasures can defeat both. [Pause]

Five — and this is the actionable insight: Trusted Execution Environments are the only currently viable path to verifiable LLM inference. They are provable, deployable today, and efficient.

[Scan Room] The call to action: model integrity guarantees should be cryptographic, not contractual. The research community should push for TEE-backed attestation as a standard requirement in commercial LLM API agreements.

Key points: (1) Complete summary of failure modes and the single viable solution (2) TEEs are the actionable recommendation (3) Community should treat this as an infrastructure standard, not an optional add-on
Duration: 2 minutes

[Benchmark] At p=0.1, you need roughly 10,000 queries. At p=0.01, you need roughly 1 million. At p→0, no fixed query budget is sufficient. Providers can always choose p small enough to stay below any detection threshold.

The second countermeasure is benchmark evasion: detect audit-specific prompts by semantic similarity and route them to the genuine model. Regular traffic gets the substitute.

Key points: (1) Randomized routing makes detection query-prohibitive as p→0 (2) O(1/p²) query budget growth — always defeatable (3) Benchmark evasion targets the detection mechanism itself
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 07_software_methods_summary

[Transition] We've now examined all three software-based detection approaches individually. This matrix puts them side by side to show the common structural failure.

Text-based statistical tests fail because FP8 outputs are nearly indistinguishable, and randomized routing defeats any fixed query budget. Log-probability fingerprinting fails because production nondeterminism makes legitimate variation indistinguishable from substitution. And all methods are rendered moot by adversarial countermeasures that any motivated provider can deploy. [Pause]

[Benchmark] The conclusion is not that these methods are poorly designed — they are reasonable attempts given the constraints. The conclusion is that the constraint itself — relying on observable outputs from a black-box API — is fundamentally incompatible with the security guarantee required.

[Scan Room] This sets up the question: if software methods cannot work, what can?

Key points: (1) Three failure modes, each independently fatal (2) Adversarial countermeasures compound all three (3) The fundamental constraint is the black-box API architecture, not the specific method
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_tee_solution

[Transition] The answer is to exit the software-only paradigm entirely. Trusted Execution Environments solve the problem at the architectural level.

A TEE — specifically NVIDIA Confidential Computing on H100 GPUs — creates a hardware-secured enclave. The provider runs inference inside the enclave, and the hardware generates a cryptographic attestation proving that specific model weights are loaded and specific inference code is executing. [Pause]

[Data] Unlike ZKPs, which are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale — they would take hours to verify a single inference pass — TEEs introduce only modest performance overhead. They are deployable today.

[Benchmark] The critical difference from all software methods: TEE attestation is not statistical evidence, it is cryptographic proof. A motivated provider cannot fake it. Hardware enforces what contracts cannot.

---

One: model substitution is economically motivated and structurally enabled. This is not a hypothetical threat — it's a rational business decision under current API architecture.
